name: Academy Arc
title: Setup, workflow & proof of work
boss: A working toolkit, a public learning-log repository and one short analysis of a clean sample CSV.
intro: Start where you are: Excel experience and early SQL practice. This is a diagnostic and setup week, not a restart from zero.
items: Check your device: Power BI Desktop requires Windows; arrange Windows access if using a Mac.
Set up Excel or Microsoft 365 access; identify which Power Query features your version supports.
Choose one SQL learning environment: browser for basics, PostgreSQL + DBeaver/VS Code for the main course. Use SQL Server only for the short Microsoft bridge.
Create folders: raw-data, cleaned-data, sql, notebooks, reports and screenshots.
Create GitHub profile + learning-log repository; upload a README and a sample SQL file.
Learn Git status, add, commit, pull and push, or use GitHub’s web upload first.
Set a repeatable 12-hour weekly schedule around your work, study and other commitments.
Record your baseline: one PivotTable, one SELECT query and a 60-second explanation.
Use only public or synthetic practice data; never upload confidential employer, customer or colleague information.
Write one analysis question with a metric, time period and intended reader.
Identify personal/sensitive data, check the permitted purpose, and use only approved public or synthetic practice files.
Record ten genuine employer adverts: verify location, level, essential criteria, closing date and whether it is a paid job rather than a fee-charging course.
rule: If setup takes more than a session, use browser tools and keep practising. Tool installation is not the boss.

name: Foundation Arc
title: Excel Pro & Power Query
boss: Project 1: a refreshable retail workbook with raw/clean tabs, PivotTables and a one-page recommendation.
intro: Build on what you already know. Spend less time watching familiar material and more time explaining how you checked the result.
resources: Excel for Data Analytics — Full Course
Luke Barousse · ~11h · English · watch selected chapters
items: Clean like a pro: Duplicates, TRIM, flash fill
Formulas: IF, SUMIFS, TEXT/DATE
Lookups: VLOOKUP → XLOOKUP → INDEX/MATCH
PivotTables: Group by month, slicers, PivotChart
Power Query: Unpivot, merge, refresh
Dashboard: 1 interactive dashboard answering a business Q
Use Excel Tables, structured references and consistent data types.
Handle blanks, errors and dates with UK locale; distinguish missing values from zero.
Check XLOOKUP exact matches and unmatched keys; explain one-to-many lookup limits.
Calculate revenue, units, average basket and percentage change with explicit definitions.
Reconcile row counts and sales totals before and after cleaning.
Write three findings and one limitation; label synthetic data clearly.
Close the tutorial and rebuild your main PivotTable without help.
Export a readable dashboard PDF and document refresh steps.
Build an exceptions tab showing failed checks; add conditional formatting and data validation where useful.
Combine two monthly CSV files with Power Query, keep a source-file column, and test a later refresh.
rule: Your boss test: someone else can replace the CSV and refresh the report without calling you.

name: Chakra Control Arc
title: SQL for reliable answers
boss: Project 2: a small retail database, 30 documented queries and a 30-minute closed-book SQL test.
intro: Use SQL to retrieve, combine and validate data. Practise the reasoning behind the query, not just the syntax.
resources: SQL for Data Analytics — foundations + project
Luke Barousse · ~4h · PostgreSQL; free video and starter files
Luke Barousse · ~6h full video; select gaps only, not a second compulsory binge
Microsoft Learn · free official gap lesson
Microsoft Learn · select relevant querying modules; optional local setup
items: Foundations: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, NULLs
Aggregations: COUNT/SUM/AVG, GROUP BY, HAVING, CASE
JOINs: INNER/LEFT/FULL/UNION — understand preserved rows
Window: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG/LEAD, PARTITION BY
Project: 10 queries to GitHub (retail or Northwind sample)
Understand primary/foreign keys, row grain and duplicate keys.
Filter dates safely with half-open intervals and explicit date formats.
Use IS NULL, COALESCE and NULLIF; explain COUNT(*) vs COUNT(column).
Demonstrate how a one-to-many join can inflate totals.
Write and explain a subquery and a CTE solving the same problem.
Find top products per category with a ranking window.
Calculate month-on-month change with LAG and handle missing months.
Find unmatched rows with LEFT JOIN + IS NULL or NOT EXISTS.
Explain WHERE vs HAVING; UNION vs UNION ALL.
Save 30 queries with questions, expected outputs and reconciliation checks.
Complete a timed test without copying; review mistakes the following day.
Translate five existing queries to T-SQL and explain TOP vs LIMIT, date functions and FULL OUTER JOIN support.
Calculate a running total with an explicit ROWS frame and explain how ties affect ranking.
Read a simple query plan and distinguish a view from a temporary table; leave production tuning and database administration for later.
rule: Use PostgreSQL for the main course. Spend a short bridge session translating TOP/LIMIT, GETDATE/CURRENT_DATE and DATEADD/DATEDIFF; do not install or master multiple database servers at once.

name: Power-up Arc
title: Power BI, modelling & DAX
boss: Project 3: a retail performance dashboard with a star schema, validated measures and a 3-minute demo.
intro: The hero skill is not adding charts. It is producing trustworthy measures and a page that helps a manager make one decision.
resources: Power BI for Data Analytics — Full Course
Microsoft Learn · current skills guide, not a claim of full exam readiness
items: Get Data: Power Query clean/unpivot
Model: Star schema, date table
DAX: SUM, DIVIDE, CALCULATE and filter context
Visuals: KPI cards, slicers, drill-through and accessible labels
Publish: Understand Service, sharing and refresh limitations
Portfolio: Retail dashboard + README + screenshots
Build fact sales and product/date/store dimensions with unique keys.
Use one-to-many relationships and explain filter direction.
Distinguish measures, calculated columns and Power Query steps.
Create a complete date table and consistent time intelligence measures.
Validate at least five KPI totals against Excel or SQL.
Show prior-period comparison only when date coverage is comparable.
Add clear units, source date, metric definitions and caveats.
Test slicers, drill-through, blank values and zero denominators.
Understand that Publish to web is public: only use non-sensitive public/synthetic data.
Provide PDF/screenshots + demo if you cannot share a live report.
Start a small number of targeted applications once Projects 1–3 are explainable.
Explain Import vs DirectQuery, when an on-premises gateway is needed, and what can cause scheduled refresh to fail.
Create a simple row-level security role in Desktop and use View as to test it with synthetic data.
Explain workspace roles, Viewer vs editing permissions, and why Publish to web is not secure sharing.
Use Performance Analyzer once; remove unnecessary columns and investigate a slow visual.
Configure a tooltip/bookmark or navigation button, then test keyboard access, contrast and a mobile report layout.
rule: Power BI Desktop authoring is free; some sharing and refresh options need licences. A paid subscription is not a prerequisite for portfolio evidence.

name: Analyst Thinking Arc
title: Statistics, quality & storytelling
boss: A one-page decision brief: one question, three checked findings, a recommendation and limitations.
intro: Use these ideas throughout every project; these two weeks consolidate them. This is analytics, not a machine-learning detour.
items: Statistics: Mean, median, standard deviation and outliers
Correlation: Correlation ≠ causation; confounding
Story: Question → evidence → recommendation → limitation
Choose an appropriate denominator and avoid averaging averages.
Distinguish percentage change from percentage-point change.
Recognise sampling bias, selection bias and small sample problems.
Explain confidence intervals and uncertainty in plain English.
Describe a basic A/B test, control group and random assignment.
Check whether seasonality, missing periods or population changes affect comparisons.
Use bar/line charts appropriately and avoid misleading axis scales.
Define a KPI with unit, grain, owner, period and source.
Practise a 90-second explanation for a non-technical manager.
Apply a practical UK GDPR checklist: purpose, minimisation, accuracy, retention, access and accountability; escalate uncertainty to the data owner.
Define a reporting request with audience, KPI formula, source, deadline and two acceptance checks; this is analyst practice, not a Business Analyst syllabus.
If using AI to explain a query, use synthetic examples, verify the output independently and never paste confidential work data into an unapproved tool.
rule: Never tick a finding until you can say what would make it wrong.

name: Automation Arc
title: Python, pandas & reproducibility
boss: Project 4: a reproducible public-data analysis and a script that turns a raw CSV into a checked summary report.
intro: Add Python after Excel, SQL and Power BI. Do not delay suitable applications because you have not finished a Python playlist.
resources: Python for Data Analytics — Full Course
Luke Barousse · ~11h · English · select relevant chapters
items: Python: Variables, lists, dictionaries, loops and functions
pandas: Read CSV, inspect, filter and select
Clean: Missing values, duplicates and data types
Analyse: groupby, merge, pivot_table
Visualise: Matplotlib or Seaborn with readable labels
Project: Notebook + README + reproducible outputs
Create a virtual environment and record package requirements.
Parse dates explicitly; inspect UK/US date ambiguity.
Validate merge keys and check row counts before/after joins.
Write reusable functions for load, clean, validate and export.
Use assertions for totals, unique keys and non-negative values where appropriate.
Export clean CSV + an Excel summary without overwriting raw files.
Re-run from a clean environment or a fresh Colab session.
Keep secrets and personal data out of notebooks and version control.
Create a tiny test fixture with known outputs to check one cleaning function and one aggregation.
Document relative paths, package versions and input/output filenames so another person can rerun the script.
rule: One working automation is worth more than ten copied notebooks. Measure runtime or manual steps honestly; do not invent hours saved.

name: Final Boss Arc
title: An end-to-end analytics capstone
boss: Project 5: an East Sussex public-data brief connecting SQL, a checked dataset and a Power BI dashboard, with a 5-minute walkthrough.
intro: Combine skills you already learned. Choose a question you can defend, rather than adding more tools.
resources: Official public data · select a manageable CSV
items: Choose one question: how has a selected local indicator changed over time?
Record source URL, download date, licence, geography and definitions.
Write a data dictionary and identify the grain of every table.
Keep immutable raw files and scripted cleaning steps.
Use SQL to answer at least eight meaningful questions.
Cross-check dashboard totals against SQL and an independent Excel calculation.
Explain missing data, boundary changes and incomparable time periods.
Create a concise dashboard with context, clear units and accessible colours.
Write a one-page insight brief, separating evidence from assumptions.
Document setup, refresh steps and known limitations in the README.
Record a 3–5 minute walkthrough: question, data, checks, insight, action.
Ask someone to reproduce one number and incorporate their feedback.
Polish your best three projects; keep two smaller ones as supporting evidence.
Create a one-page report runbook: owner, metric definitions, lineage, refresh timing, checks and what to do when the source changes.
Keep a short change log and have another person test the two acceptance checks before you call the report complete.
rule: A reproducible analysis with caveats beats an attractive dashboard with unexplained numbers.

name: Boss Dialogue Arc
title: SQL tests & interview confidence
boss: Two timed SQL mocks, one Excel task, one dashboard critique and four truthful STAR stories.
intro: Build this habit earlier with short weekly practice. These weeks focus on presenting evidence clearly under time pressure.
resources: Practice · some questions may require an account
items: Explain a LEFT JOIN and demonstrate duplicate-row inflation aloud.
Complete two 30-minute SQL mocks and revisit every error.
Complete an Excel clean → lookup → pivot task from a fresh file.
Explain row context, filter context and CALCULATE using your report.
Present your flagship project in five minutes without reading notes.
Prepare a truthful 60-second introduction connecting your background, analytics practice and target role.
Write four STAR stories: quality, teamwork, prioritisation and difficult customer.
State limitations and what you would investigate next.
Practise asking clarifying questions before starting a take-home task.
Prepare questions on data quality, onboarding, tools and success measures.
Rehearse a salary conversation using the advert’s range and role scope.
Use one person specification to build an evidence-to-criteria matrix, including genuine gaps, before writing a supporting statement.
rule: A gap is not a failure: explain what you know, what you would check and how you would test it.

name: Endgame Arc
title: Applications, referrals & feedback
boss: A sustainable weekly pipeline, tailored CV and project links; iterate on real feedback rather than waiting for perfection.
intro: Applications can begin in week 13. Weeks 26–28 are a focused search sprint, not a promise that an offer arrives on a deadline.
resources: Check essential criteria and application format
Use wider geography and related role titles too
items: Set alerts for Junior Data Analyst, MI Analyst, Reporting Analyst and BI Assistant.
Search Eastbourne, Lewes, Brighton/Hove and hybrid roles with a realistic commute.
Make a shortlist of ten employers; confirm vacancies on their own careers pages.
Write an ATS-readable CV with Excel, SQL, Power BI and project links near the top.
Describe your employment status accurately; list a role as current only while you still hold it.
Apply to around five well-matched roles per week when available; adjust to supply and rota.
Send two personalised networking/referral messages per week without spamming.
Track date, criteria, CV version, follow-up, outcome and feedback.
Follow up once when appropriate and respect no-contact instructions.
After 15–20 matched applications without screens, review CV, eligibility and targeting.
Practise weekly while applying; do not restart a new bootcamp after each rejection.
Check salary, hours, location, employment status and any right-to-work/sponsorship conditions.
Keep learning and searching beyond week 28 if needed; extend the timeline, not the guilt.
Create separate saved searches for Brighton/Hove, SE London boroughs, and wider-London roles; assess each commute from your actual home.
Check Level 3 Data Technician / Level 4 Data Analyst apprenticeships where eligible; verify each advert’s qualifications, residency/funding and existing-qualification rules.
rule: No guaranteed conversion rate. Your targets are controllable actions; interview and offer outcomes are not.
